name: Ascension

card.summary: Community term for a large improvement in one's looks over time; the word describes an outcome, not a specific method.
card.note: Methods members associate with ascension vary widely and include some with documented medical risks, covered in their own entries.

quick.overview:
In looksmaxxing slang, ascension means a marked rise in perceived attractiveness, often shown through before-and-after photos. Members post ascension plans, protocols and progress updates on looksmax.org.

The term is a label for an outcome, so there is no single treatment or study behind it. What people do in pursuit of it ranges from grooming and fitness to medical interventions.
quick.mechanism: There is no single mechanism. Members describe combining changes such as body-fat loss, skin, hair, dental or surgical work, and in some cases hormones, depending on the plan.
quick.risks: Risks depend entirely on the methods used. Some forum posts describe emotional outcomes: one thread title holds that ascension will not cure psychological issues.

lead: Ascension is looksmaxxing community slang for a substantial improvement in a person's looks, and the verb ascend is used for someone undertaking one. Looksmax.org has many threads titled with the word, including plans, protocols with promised before-and-after photos, and long progress updates [1][2][3].

The term is not a procedure, product or theory. Posts show members using it for outcomes reached through body-fat loss, among other routes, and for emotional reactions to looking better; one poster describes crying from joy after losing weight and no longer feeling subhuman, a framing other members questioned [1]. A thread titled to the effect that ascension will not cure psychological issues shows the community also debates its limits [4].
infobox: Looksmax.org threads: ascension plans, protocols, updates

paras: Members use ascension both as a noun for the change itself and as a goal-setting frame, as in threads named for an ascension plan with a target year [5]. The scope of what counts varies from a single change such as weight loss to multi-year plans.

Threads include requests for ratings after changes, protocol posts promising before-and-after photos, and reflective posts on the emotions of ascending [1][2][3][4]. The reflective thread cited here treats emotional release as a sign of a significant change, and a reply suggests the poster's weight loss may have influenced his mood [1].
Not all discussion is positive: at least one thread argues that ascension does not resolve psychological problems [4].
No studies found. Ascension is a slang label rather than an intervention, so there is no trial of it as such.

lore.intro: Members use the term for appearance outcomes and the emotional meaning attached to them [1][4].

claims.claim: A successful ascension is accompanied by strong emotion and reflection on one's past self.
claims.believers: One poster says anyone who has not cried or reflected after ascending did not ascend enough, citing his own experience after weight loss [1].
claims.experts: No published studies examine this claim.

claims.claim: Ascension does not fix psychological problems.
claims.believers: A thread titled to that effect argues that looking better does not address underlying psychological issues [4].
claims.experts: No published studies are cited on the effect of appearance-changing procedures on psychological issues in the looksmaxxing context.
